Respiration consumes oxygen rather than producing it as a by-product.
Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from plants, not oxygen production.
Fermentation does not produce oxygen as a by-product.
Photosynthesis releases oxygen as a by-product.
At about 40–45°C, very high temperature can cause transpiration to stop as stomata close.
10–20°C is not the temperature range at which transpiration stops.
30–40°C is not the usual stated stopping range for transpiration.

Anatomy studies the structure of organisms, especially internal structure.
Histology is the microscopic study of tissues.
Morphology studies the form and external structure of organisms.
Entomology is the study of insects.
Deductions are the logical consequences drawn from a hypothesis.
A theory is a well-supported explanation, not the consequences of a hypothesis.
A law describes a consistently observed natural relationship.
Experiments test a hypothesis rather than name its logical consequences.
Order is a taxonomic rank above family.
Family is a taxonomic rank above genus and species.
Species is the basic unit of biological classification.
Class is a taxonomic rank above order.
Linnaeus classified nature into three kingdoms: animal, plant, and mineral.
Five kingdoms were proposed in a later classification system, not by Linnaeus.
Seven is not the number of kingdoms in Linnaeus’s classification of nature.
Ten is not the number of kingdoms in Linnaeus’s classification of nature.
Robert Brown is known for describing the cell nucleus, not the dark reactions.
Louis Pasteur studied fermentation and microorganisms, not the dark reactions.
Aristotle was an ancient philosopher and naturalist, not the discoverer of the dark reactions.
Melvin Calvin and his colleagues elucidated the details of the dark reactions.
Mitochondria are the main sites of aerobic respiration in eukaryotic cells.
Plastids are mainly involved in functions such as photosynthesis and storage.
Lysosomes digest cellular materials and are not sites of aerobic respiration.
Centrioles help organize cell division and are not sites of aerobic respiration.
Connective tissue supports, binds, or connects body structures.
Muscle tissue is specialized for contraction and movement.
Nervous tissue is composed mainly of nerve cells and supporting cells.
Epithelial tissue covers body surfaces and lines cavities.
Apoptotic bodies are fragments formed as the apoptotic cell breaks apart.
Blebs are irregular bulges of the cell membrane formed during apoptosis.
Chromatin bodies are not the name for the membrane buds formed during apoptosis.
Tumors are abnormal masses of cells, not apoptotic membrane buds.
Enzymes are generally proteins made from amino acids.
Carbohydrates are not the usual structural material of enzymes.
Lipids do not make up enzymes, although they have other cellular roles.
Vitamins may assist enzyme activity but are not what enzymes are made of.
Tissue death is necrosis, not the meaning of myocardium.
Myocardium means the muscular tissue of the heart.
An embolus is a travelling blockage in a blood vessel.
A thrombus is a blood clot formed within a blood vessel.
Ornithology is the study of birds, not entomology.
Entomology is the study of insects.
Mammalogy is the study of mammals.
Ichthyology is the study of fishes.
A principle is a general rule or fundamental truth, not the logical consequence of a hypothesis.
An observation is information gathered through the senses or instruments.
A result is an outcome, but the specific logical consequence of a hypothesis is a deduction.
A deduction is a logical consequence drawn from a hypothesis.
